title: The Wrong Door
story: The ticket machine should say Exact change for exactly 10 coins, Overpaid for more, Not enough for fewer. It is broken in two ways.
goal: Fix the program so all three cases work.
starter:
coins = int(input())
if coins >= 10:
    print("Exact change")
elif coins > 10
    print("Overpaid")
else:
    print("Not enough")
hints: Run it first. Python complains about one line. What is missing at the end of an elif line?
Once it runs, try 11 coins. Which branch answers? Is >= the same as "exactly"?
socratic: What must every if/elif/else line end with?
For 11 coins, which condition is true first?
explain: In one sentence: what is the difference between >= and ==?
